case.summary: Alert HHF-002 opened because an analyst asked for a review of transaction 3660127 and related activity on other cards ($770.78, product C, online, 2017-01-19 18:18) on card C06220-K1. Assessed as an undocumented coordinated pattern with fraud probability 0.97. Main findings: The same template appears on 14 other cards within 14 days, none sharing a device with this card: coordinated abuse across customers. The episode covers 3 transaction(s) totalling $2,166.71, and 14 other card(s) are linked by a repeated template of product C purchases of $200 or more in bursts from devices marked New behind an anonymous proxy, with no shared device. Actions: block card, create case, file report, monitor connected cards, escalate to analyst. Evidence request: Customer states they did not make these purchases and still has the card.

sar.narrative: This report concerns customer C06220, card C06220-K1, issued as a visa credit. Between 2017-01-17 and 2017-01-19, 3 transaction(s) totalling $2,166.71 were identified as part of one fraud episode, beginning with transaction 3660125. The activity took place online, product code(s) C, billing region(s) 126, 330, 384, from device profile(s) SM-J700T1 |  |  | ; SM-J700T1 | iOS 11.1.1 | mobile safari 11.0 | 2048x1536. The transactions were bursts of online purchases from devices new to the account behind an anonymous proxy, the same template appearing on other customers' cards with no device in common. The activity is assessed as an undocumented coordinated pattern: The same template appears on 14 other cards within 14 days, none sharing a device with this card: coordinated abuse across customers. The shared element (a repeated template of product C purchases of $200 or more in bursts from devices marked New behind an anonymous proxy, with no shared device) links this activity to 14 other card(s), including C00450-K1, C02342-K1, C03528-K1, C05061-K1, which indicates a common actor across cardholders. Earlier confirmed cases CC-3077, CC-1969, CC-0626 show the same pattern. When contacted, the cardholder stated they did not make the transaction(s), did not share the card details, and still has the card. The bank has recommended BLOCK_CARD, MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS and opened an internal case; the report is filed under R9, §3a.

stop_reason: The customer's reply settled the question (section 6): probability moved from 0.82 to 0.97 and the episode (3 transaction(s), $2,166.71) is scoped. Further steps would not change the actions.
